new.back: To aim for something, to intend it
new.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: tayammum — class notes 2026-10-14

new.back: Wiping the face, and the arms up to the elbows, with earth, with the intention of purification — the aim is not to put dirt on oneself
new.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: tayammum — class notes 2026-10-14

new.front: Where in the Qurʾān is tayammum legislated?
new.back: Sūrat al-Māʾidah: <bdi>فَلَمْ تَجِدُوا مَاءً فَتَيَمَّمُوا صَعِيدًا طَيِّبًا</bdi> — “and you find no water, then seek clean earth” (5:6)
new.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: tayammum — class notes 2026-10-14

new.front: What was the occasion for the revelation of tayammum?
new.back: On a journey, ʿĀʾishah's necklace broke and was lost. The Prophet ﷺ and the people stayed to search for it where there was no water, and Abū Bakr came and rebuked her. They woke with still no water, and Allah revealed tayammum.
new.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: tayammum — class notes 2026-10-14

new.front: According to Abū Dharr's ḥadīth, for how long is clean earth a purifier for a Muslim who finds no water?
new.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: tayammum — class notes 2026-10-14

new.front: What did the Prophet ﷺ say of the earth, in Abū Umāmah's ḥadīth?
new.back: That the whole of it is a masjid and a purifier
new.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: tayammum — class notes 2026-10-14

new.back: Both the minor and the major ritual impurity — <bdi>الحَدَث الأَصْغَر</bdi> and <bdi>الحَدَث الأَكْبَر</bdi> — so it stands in for ghusl as well as wuḍūʾ
new.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: tayammum — class notes 2026-10-14

new.front: How far must water be before it counts as unavailable for tayammum?
new.back: About a mile or more — roughly a half-hour walk
new.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: tayammum — class notes 2026-10-14

new.text: Tayammum is allowed when one is unable to use water, as with {{c1::cold so extreme that one fears illness or injury, with no way to heat the water}}; {{c2::sickness}}; or {{c3::fear of thirst}}
new.extra: The other ground is that water is unavailable — about a mile or more away.
new.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: tayammum — class notes 2026-10-14

new.front: Which prayers may one make tayammum for, though water is at hand, for fear of missing them?
new.back: The funeral prayer, if one is not the deceased's walī, and the ʿīd prayer — for the Ḥanafīs neither has a replacement or a make-up
new.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: tayammum — class notes 2026-10-14

new.front: Why does fear of missing the Friday prayer not allow tayammum, when fear of missing the ʿīd prayer does?
new.back: Jumuʿah has a replacement — ẓuhr. One makes wuḍūʾ, and prays ẓuhr if Jumuʿah is missed.
new.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: tayammum — class notes 2026-10-14

new.front: What may tayammum be made with, for the Ḥanafīs?
new.back: Any pure substance of the earth that does not burn to ash and is not a metal — soil, sand, stone
new.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: tayammum — class notes 2026-10-14

new.front: How does the intention in tayammum differ from the intention in wuḍūʾ, for the Ḥanafīs?
new.back: In tayammum it is obligatory; in wuḍūʾ it is only recommended (qud-168) — fittingly, <bdi>تَيَمُّم</bdi> itself means to intend
new.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: tayammum — class notes 2026-10-14

new.text: Tayammum, in order: {{c1::make the intention}}; {{c2::strike the material once and wipe the whole face}}; {{c3::strike it a second time and wipe the arms, from the fingertips up to and including the elbows — right, then left}}
new.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṭahārah: tayammum — class notes 2026-10-14

new.front: On what must the answer to any Islamic question be based?
new.source: Arbaʿīn / Qudūrī — ikhtilāf: the strength of evidence — class notes 2026-10-14
Arbaʿīn / Qudūrī — ikhtilāf: the strength of evidence — class notes 2026-10-14

new.meaning: speculative — of evidence, short of certain, though it can still be very strong
new.source: Arbaʿīn / Qudūrī — ikhtilāf: the strength of evidence — class notes 2026-10-14

new.meaning: a proof's transmission — how it reached us: by tawātur, or as āḥād
new.source: Arbaʿīn / Qudūrī — ikhtilāf: the strength of evidence — class notes 2026-10-14

new.meaning: a proof's signification — how clear its meaning is, and whether it is open to interpretation
new.source: Arbaʿīn / Qudūrī — ikhtilāf: the strength of evidence — class notes 2026-10-14

new.front: What is the highest standard of evidence?
new.back: <bdi>قَطْعِيّ الثُّبُوت وَقَطْعِيّ الدَّلَالَة</bdi> — transmitted by tawātur, with a meaning not open to interpretation
new.source: Arbaʿīn / Qudūrī — ikhtilāf: the strength of evidence — class notes 2026-10-14

new.text: Disagreement is allowed where a proof is ẓannī in some respect: <bdi>قَطْعِيّ الثُّبُوت، ظَنِّيّ الدَّلَالَة</bdi> — {{c1::its source is certain, but people differ on its meaning}}; <bdi>ظَنِّيّ الثُّبُوت، قَطْعِيّ الدَّلَالَة</bdi> — {{c2::its meaning is clear, but its transmission is weaker}}; <bdi>ظَنِّيّ الثُّبُوت، ظَنِّيّ الدَّلَالَة</bdi> — {{c3::both are speculative}}
new.extra: Only the qaṭʿī–qaṭʿī proof leaves no room for disagreement.
new.source: Arbaʿīn / Qudūrī — ikhtilāf: the strength of evidence — class notes 2026-10-14

new.front: How certain is a ẓannī proof, compared with a qaṭʿī one?
new.back: A qaṭʿī proof is 100% certain. A ẓannī one is not, but its certainty can still be very high — ẓannī doesn't mean 0%.
new.source: Arbaʿīn / Qudūrī — ikhtilāf: the strength of evidence — class notes 2026-10-14
